title: The Quiet Clock's Song
markdown:
In a little house, snuggly and comfy between a field that loved to whisper secrets to the wind and a forest full of trees that stood like friendly sleepy giants, lived a dalmatian pup named Dottie. Dottie was a fluffy white cloud with big black happy spots, like someone had spilled a whole bunch of chocolate chips. Her tail was like a happy little bouncy spring, always going wag-wag-wag. And right next door, in the cool leafy shade where the sunbeams played peek-a-boo, lived a shy little fawn named Fern. Fern had eyes as soft as moss on a log and ears that could hear a ladybug sneeze.

One evening, the sky was putting on its best pajamas, changing from sleepy pink to a gentle calming purple. Dottie and Fern were playing near the big nursery window. This was their favourite spot because it had a clock. And this clock went tick-tock, tick-tock. It sounded like a little heart beating, saying it was time for sleepy cuddles and happy dreams.

But tonight the tick-tock was gone. The clock was quiet. Super quiet. Quieter than a mouse tiptoeing on marshmallows.

“Oh, no,” whispered Fern, her soft ears drooping a little, like tired flower petals. “The clock isn’t ticking. It’s too quiet for sleepy time. How will we know when it’s time for snuggles?”

Dottie nudged Fern with her cool wet nose. A little rumble of hmmmm came from her tummy. “We need to find a new sound,” she woofed, a tiny questioning ruff that floated in the air. “A sound to help the clock remember its sleepy song.”

They sat, thinking and thinking. Their little noses twitched. Dottie tried a little woof-woof, a soft rumbling sound that came from her happy spot. “Woof… woof…” she tried, her tail giving just one slow hopeful wag. It was a nice sound, a happy sound, but it wasn’t the clock’s special tick-tock. Fern then gently shuffled her little hooves on the soft grass, making a sound like dry leaves dancing a little jig. “Shhh, shhh, shhh,” she whispered, hoping the quiet clock would listen. But the clock just sat there, quiet as a sleepy cloud.

Then Fern’s big soft eyes lit up. She remembered a sound from long ago, a sound her mama made. It was a hum, a low gentle hum that felt warm and safe, like snuggling under a million fluffy blankets. Fern started to hum, very, very softly, a tune as sweet as a butterfly’s kiss. “Mmmmm… mmmmm…” she hummed, her voice like a tiny happy bumblebee.

Dottie listened, her floppy ears perked up. Her tail gave a slow happy wag-wag-wag. That sound was so lovely. It made her feel all warm and fuzzy. But the clock still didn’t tick. So Dottie decided to add her own little sound to Fern’s hum. She didn’t bark loud. She made a soft gentle ruff, a little ruff-ruff that seemed to fit perfectly with Fern’s hum. “Mmmmm… ruff… Mmmmm… ruff…” she whispered, making a gentle ruff-ruff-hummmm sound.

And the nursery clock, which had been so very quiet, began to whisper back. Tick… tock… tick… tock… It was a much, much softer sound than before, a gentle sleepy sound that made Dottie and Fern feel all warm and wonderfully cozy, all the way down to their wiggly toes. The clock had found its sleepy song again, all thanks to Fern’s gentle hum and Dottie’s happy ruff-ruff.

Dottie yawned a big wide sleepy yawn, her little pink tongue peeking out. Fern blinked her soft eyes slowly. The quiet had gone, and the clock’s lovely gentle lullaby was back. The big round moon peeked through the window, casting a silvery dreamy light all over the room. Dottie curled up into a soft furry ball right by the window, and Fern rested her gentle head on a soft patch of sweet-smelling clover. Soon they both drifted off to sleep, dreaming the sweetest happiest dreams, to the soothing sound of the softly ticking clock.

And so, when a sleepy song is missing, two quiet friends may find it together, one hum and one ruff at a time.
characters: Dottie (a dalmatian pup), Fern (the forest fawn)
author: StoryGen Community
